Their personal journeys reveal struggles with relationships, children, and belief.Episodes6Next episodeVideos1Featured reviewsBiblical Epic or Biblical Ooops?The cast is genuinely good, and the casting director, whose name is not currently listed on the production details here, deserves a medal for assembling such talent. As for this miniseries - The Faithful - it's a Mesopotamian Mess with British Accents!Holy Genesis, what happened here?René Echevarria, known for genuine classics: Star Trek: The Next Generation,Star Trek: Deep Space Nine,The 4400,is the executive producer (showrunner) of this miniseries, and writer of its first episode!This miniseries takes the women of the Bible - Sarah, Rebekah, Leah, Rachel, and the rest - and turns their powerful stories of faith, family, and founding three major religions into a wardrobe malfunction wrapped in a script disaster. From intolerable costumes to awful dialogue, nothing is Biblically, historically, or culturally accurate beyond the names.Mesopotamian folks rocking posh British accents, with major details getting omitted or twisted into a modern fem-tale that somehow still flops, and, too bad the rest is pure unfaithful fiction! Skip it and just read the actual Book.Not BiblicalAfter only one episode it is beyond obvious that this is a fictional retelling of the holy scriptures. Although there is a warning at the start I was still surprised at the level of fiction. Major details from Genesis are omitted changing the faith story into a story of disobedience and unfaithfulness. Very disappointing as I was very much looking forward to the whole series.Casting ChoicesImmediately based off casting alone this is getting only five stars from me. I'm okay to an extent with extra parts of the stories being addd to fill out the narrative of these women's lives because the Bible doesn't always go into some of the minute details needed to flesh a story out for TV. But Sarah should have been older than who they cast for her and all of this cast needed to be about three skin shades darker. I am tired of seeing white people with straight hair cast in roles of biblical figures when all of them were middle eastern, North African and East African and thus darker skinned because they lived on the African plate near the equator. Israel is on the African plate. If you are going to tell a story about biblical figures especially women tell it right and make sure the actors reflect what the people looked like around that time. That is so important especially for people of color who struggle to see themselves in the Bible when they were there all along.A Biblical DisasterDisappointed in this series. I watched the first episode with a friend and commented throughout the episode, "that's not what happened." After each commercial, I read her the biblical text to show her what actually happened.The only positive part of this series is the cast. I think they did a good job despite the script's false narrative.DisappointedI was so excited to see the Genesis story of these women come alive but VERY disappointed with the amount of content that pulls away from the true storyline. Example: Sarai saying she bows to no man, Sarai snatched by the Pharoah and decides on her own to say she is the sister of her husband, pharoah getting a bloody nose then returning her, and the amount of immodesty with the Egyptian slave was NOT needed! No way would she have walked around Abram's camp with her boobs hanging out! Deleted recordings- not continuing.
